subject: Pinebrook evaluation — fidelity checks, exit gates, and MAP action ladder
messages:
From: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@pinebrook.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@pinebrook.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft and acceptance criteria (Pinebrook evaluation)

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with latency and the explainability hooks. We want to accelerate the evaluation and get to a customer acceptance decision within the next 4 weeks. Attached is the MAP draft we started internally (Pinebrook_MAP_v1.xlsx). Can you and your team propose a concise set of acceptance tests + exit gates we can run during the next two-week evaluation sprint?

High-level asks from our side:
- Safety/concordance tolerance: false-positive rate for PHI redaction <= 1% on sample corpus (we'll share)
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 450ms for 512 token context in our staging region
- Cost: token cost estimate + suggestion for caching/batching to hit expected run rate

Please include an evidence matrix that maps each test to who runs it, expected pass criteria, and what constitutes a failed gate (and rollback). Legal looped in for any data residency notes.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Barnes
Director, Data Platforms | Pinebrook Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@pinebrook.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft and acceptance criteria (Pinebrook evaluation)

Tom — thanks, and great meeting. I pulled together a focused acceptance playbook and evidence plan (attached: redwood-eval-acceptance-tests.md). High level proposal below — short, runnable, and mapped to the MAP timeline.

Acceptance tiers (P0 / P1 / P2) — what must pass to move forward:
- P0 (blocker) — Data safety and privacy:
  - PHI redaction concordance >= 99% on Pinebrook sample (automated script + manual review 100-sample)
  - Customer-controlled KV/prefix caching disabled by default; no data persisted to shared cache
- P1 (go/no-go gating metrics):
  - Latency: 95p < 420ms for 512-token (staging infra matching your region)
  - Throughput: 200 concurrent sessions with < 2% tail failure rate for 1-minute stress test
  - Model quality: top-1 accuracy on 50 labeled prompts >= 88% (your rubric)
- P2 (operational comfort):
  - Cost projection within 10% of estimate with recommended batching settings
  - Telemetry: Token-level cost traces and per-route latency in the console

Exit gates and what failing means:
- If any P0 fails: immediate stop; Redwood to triage within 24h and propose mitigation. If unresolved in 72h, evaluation is paused and rollback to baseline model is instantiated.
- If P1 partially fails (<=1 metric missed): can proceed to extended trial if a technical remediation plan is documented and committed to within 5 business days.
- Multiple P1 failures or P1 failure for latency/throughput: pause and require lab re-run.

Test ownership and evidence matrix (short):
- Pinebrook: provide labeled prompts, sample corpus for PHI test, and legal confirmation on masked examples.
- Redwood (Hannah/Ben): run latency and throughput stress tests in your staging VPC; provide traces, Grafana links, and token-cost calc.
- Joint: manual review of PHI redaction 100-sample, signoff form.

Timeline (two-week sprint):
- Week 1 (Thu 6/19–Wed 6/25): Data handoff, baseline runs, PHI script run, initial latency profile.
- Week 2 (Thu 6/26–Wed 7/2): Remediation runs, manual review, final cost projection, sign-off meeting on Fri 7/4.

Action items I propose now:
1) Pinebrook to share sample corpus + labeled 50 prompts by EOD Thu 6/19.
2) Ben to schedule a 90-minute runbook test window with our infra team (we can do Tue 6/24 or Wed 6/25).
3) Legal/Legal contact to confirm masked sample acceptability (cc'd) — any residency concerns call them out now.

Attaching the acceptance-tests doc and a one-page evidence matrix. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
